units.spine: Market day is when Rundgate is most itself, and the roads bring in the custom that gives the stalls their reason for standing.
Armed order is part of the town's furniture, and professionals are kept for its safety rather than trusting to luck or its neighbours.
People in Rundgate can afford to argue about things other than money.
The town expects to go on being itself.
Rundgate is defended properly rather than impressively, and the works are sound without being for show.
A real body of armed men stands ready on the walls, and they look as though they have done this before.
Children here are taught the rules about the dark early, and the rules work.
Reports that reach the watch get answered, and nothing further is sought out.
Prices are steady in a way that suggests the town is not living on the last thing it sold.
Somebody here can do what is usually needed and knows what is beyond them.
Nobody in Rundgate spends a thought on food.
Sitting on the way to somewhere has given the town a modest living.
The road brings in what the town cannot grow, and the town's life depends on the road staying open.
Grown large, the town now has quarters that do not all know each other.
The town has faced pressure enough to bend its ties to its neighbours, and they have not bent.
